finding.claim: Stored SSRF: callbackUrl supplied to POST /subscribe is saved without any validation and later requested server-side by notifyAll every minute, with the payload as POST body. An attacker can target internal services, localhost, or cloud metadata (http://169.254.169.254/), and can also hit arbitrary internal hosts repeatedly.
finding.sink: HttpClient.send with HttpRequest built from URI.create(cb) in Jobs.notifyAll

trace.note: URL stored in subscriptions map with no scheme/host/IP validation
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, or DNS pinning anywhere on the path. Only URI.create syntax parsing. Response is discarded, so it is blind SSRF (but still a request-forgery with attacker-controlled destination and a POST body). The thumb() method (line 29-35) was also checked: it uses a fully anchored String.matches regex pinned to https://cdn.example.com/img/[a-z0-9]+.png, which does not allow userinfo, other hosts, or path tricks, and HttpClient defaults to no redirect following, so it is not reported.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 sends a POST to URI.create(cb) with no scheme, host or IP check. The only route is the commented POST /subscribe; no auth or middleware exists in the repo, so authentication is unverified. The regex at line 30 guards thumb() only.
